title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document describes Redwood Inference’s standard practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, interviewers, and all people managers. The procedures below are the company standard; exceptions must be approved by People Ops and the manager’s director.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Purpose: hire predictably, reduce bias, speed time-to-offer, and ensure candidate experience and legal compliance.

Owner: people-ops (recruiting), hiring manager (role definition and interview loop).

Key outputs: role brief, scorecard, interview loop, approved offer, onboarding plan.

Steps (standard):
1. Role brief and approval
   - Hiring manager fills the Role Brief template and publishes to the shared Hiring Tracker. Include: level, compensation band, remote/office, required skills, diversity goals, and expected start date.
   - People Ops reviews and approves headcount/compensation band within 48 business hours.

2. Sourcing and screening
   - Recruiter sources candidates (internal first, then external).
   - Initial 30-minute screen (recruiter) uses standardized screen checklist: background fit, eligibility to work, salary expectations, notice period, and basic role competencies.

3. Interview loop design & scorecard
   - Hiring manager defines a scorecard with 4–6 core competencies and weighting (e.g., technical skill 40%, onboarding potential 20%, culture fit 20%, communication 20%).
   - Interview loop should include at least: a technical assessment (take-home or live), a manager interview, a peer interview, and an interview focused on collaboration/culture. For senior roles add a cross-functional partner interview.
   - People Ops confirms loop and books interviews.

4. Interviewing & calibration
   - Interviewers read the candidate packet and rubric before the interview.
   - Use structured interview questions tied to the scorecard; capture numerical scores and qualitative notes after the interview.
   - No hiring decisions from a single interviewer; require at least 3 independent interviewer inputs for full-time roles.

5. Debrief & decision
   - Scheduling a 30–60 minute debrief within 48 hours of last interview. Hiring manager synthesizes scores and qualitative feedback to a Hiring Recommendation.
   - People Ops reviews for compensation equity and sign-off.

6. Offer & negotiation
   - People Ops drafts the offer letter (standard template) and sends it to the hiring manager for approval.
   - Recruiting leads the negotiation; changes to base beyond band or material equity deviations require Director approval.

7. Background checks & finalization
   - Conditional offer contingent on background check and references. Recruiting coordinates checks and confirms start date.

Hiring best-practices & compliance notes:
- Use standardized scorecards to reduce bias.
- All interview feedback must be submitted in the ATS within 24 hours.
- For roles that handle sensitive customer data or require clearance, add an identity verification step and security interview.
- Keep candidate communications timely: initial reply <72 hours; offer after final decision within 72 hours.

2) New hire onboarding (0–90 days)

Objective: accelerate time-to-value, establish clarity on role expectations, and integrate hires into culture and systems.

Owner: Hiring manager (programmatic), People Ops (coordinator & core programs), IT & Security (access provisioning).

Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- People Ops sends Welcome packet (Welcome email, benefits link, first-week schedule).
- IT creates accounts and requests hardware shipment 10 business days before start date.
- Manager shares 30-60-90 plan and first-week agenda.

Day 1 checklist:
- Welcome meeting with manager (30 min): review role, priorities, communication norms.
- New Hire Orientation (People Ops) 90 min: company mission, org chart, benefits, HR policies, security overview.
- IT security & compliance: MFA enablement, SSO login, device security checklist.
- Team welcome and intro meeting.

First week:
- Role-specific training sessions and small first deliverable assigned.
- Shadowing & pairing on core systems.
- Checkpoint with manager day 3 and day 7.

30-60-90 plan (template):
- 30 days: learning objectives, access to systems, complete 1 small project, establish 1:1 rhythm.
- 60 days: own one incremental feature/process, demonstrate competency in core tooling, provide feedback on onboarding.
- 90 days: reach expected baseline for role level, present a 90-day summary to manager, set development goals.

Onboarding metrics & escalation:
- Targets: new hires to complete core trainings by day 14; first meaningful contribution by day 30 for ICs.
- Manager must file an At-Risk report with People Ops if progress is behind schedule at any checkpoint.

3) Performance and feedback cycles

Cadence:
- Continuous feedback: encouraged in 1:1s and project retrospectives.
- Formal cycles: Quarterly check-ins (informal), Annual performance review and calibration (documented).
- For ICs: career ladder progression reviews at least annually; for managers: leadership calibration with director.

Quarterly check-in (recommended):
- Purpose: align priorities, remove blockers, and provide developmental feedback.
- Output: updated objectives, short-term actions, and any role risk flags.

Annual performance review process (timeline):
1. Self-assessment: employee completes self-review form.
2. Manager assessment: manager submits summary and rating using the competency rubric.
3. Peer input: optional 360 feedback for roles with heavy cross-functional collaboration.
4. Calibration: People Ops runs calibration sessions by department to ensure fairness and leveling consistency.
5. Review meeting: manager meets employee to discuss rating, compensation actions, and development plan.

Rating & calibration notes:
- Use objective evidence: projects, metrics, and peer feedback.
- Calibration panels include manager, director, and a People Ops representative.
- Compensation actions (merit, promotion, equity grants) require budget owner sign-off.

4) Coaching, corrections, and performance improvement

Informal coaching:
- Immediate, private feedback; document outcomes in manager notes.

Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP):
- Triggers: repeated missed objectives, conduct issues, or SLO breaches after informal coaching.
- Process steps:
  1. Manager documents specific gaps and a measurable improvement plan (30–90 days).
  2. People Ops reviews the PIP for fairness and legal compliance.
  3. Weekly check-ins and documented evidence of progress.
  4. Closure: success (return to normal cadence) or next steps (role change or separation).

Note: PIPs are not solely punitive; they are a formal support mechanism. People Ops must be involved early.

5) Manager responsibilities and expectations

Managers are critical to hiring quality and retention. Primary responsibilities include:
- Build and maintain the interview loop and scorecards for roles on their team.
- Conduct regular 1:1s and timely feedback; keep written notes.
- Drive onboarding plans and early development goals.
- Conduct calibration-ready performance documentation (evidence-based).
- Escalate people risks to People Ops: at-risk hires, intensive support needs, or potential legal issues.

Manager checklist (quick reference):
- Before hire: complete role brief, define scorecard.
- Offer stage: approve compensation within band.
- Day 1: schedule orientation, meet & greet, share 30-60-90.
- Ongoing: weekly 1:1s, quarterly check-ins, annual reviews.

6) Templates & artifacts (location and examples)

Stored in: /shared/people-ops/templates and /confluence/company-handbook.
- Role Brief template (CSV/Google Sheet)
- Interview scorecard (standardized rubric)
- Offer letter template
- 30-60-90 plan template
- Self-review and manager review forms
- PIP template

7) Metrics and reporting

Key metrics People Ops tracks: time-to-fill, time-to-offer, acceptance rate, first-90-day retention, new hire training completion rate, manager NPS (post-onboarding survey).
- Monthly report: Recruiting funnel and diversity metrics.
- Quarterly: New hire quality (manager satisfaction), onboarding completion rates.

8) Frequently asked questions

Q: What if a manager needs to hire faster than the standard timeline?
A: Mark the requisition as expedited in the Role Brief. People Ops will prioritize but will still require scorecard and approved band.

Q: Can interviewers use their own questions?
A: Interviewers must use the standardized rubric and may add follow-ups, but core competency questions should be used to keep consistency.

Q: Where do I find support for visa or relocation?
A: Contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai) for policy and budget approvals.

Appendix: Contact list and escalation

- People Ops General: people-ops@redwood.ai
